extracted.intended_audience: Contracting Officers and government contracting personnel (Navy/DoD) involved in A-76 cost-comparison procurements
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for Contracting Officers and Task Group members on planning, milestone management, Statement of Work (SOW) preparation, solicitation clauses, integrity safeguards, and cost-comparison procedures under OMB Circular A-76 and related DoD guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for contracting personnel technical familiarization
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting personnel need to be familiarized with the technical details of A-76 type contracting; an overview of the cost comparison process is necessary for a contract negotiator to perform professionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research indicated very few personnel could answer methodological questions about evaluating cost-type proposals or incentive arrangements; training and familiarization are needed so contracting negotiators can competently participate in cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training availability and suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal training exists (e.g., a four-day Army Logistics Management Center course with a two-hour executive overview) but is mainly oriented to financial management personnel rather than Contracting Officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although somewhat beneficial, existing courses focus on those preparing government cost estimates and performing cost comparisons — areas from which the Contracting Officer should be excluded — so a dedicated in-house program based on current guidance is more appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task Group primary objective
rubrics_metrics.description: The Task Group is responsible for initiating the cost comparison, continuously monitoring progress, and driving the process to satisfactory completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting Officers should assess their level of involvement; the Task Group must steer the effort through planning, monitoring, and progressing actions to completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task Group composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial Task Group usually includes representatives from the functional/operational organization, Manpower/Personnel Office, Finance/Accounting Office, Legal Office, and Contracting Office; chairperson may vary by service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Navy the Comptroller or Planning Officer often chairs; in Air Force the Manpower Office chairs. Composition should ensure expertise for SOW, cost estimate, legal sufficiency, and contracting actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task Group milestone and deliverable responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Members must establish realistic milestones and focus first on preparing a comprehensive Statement of Work, then develop an accurate Government cost estimate, conduct the cost comparison after bids/offers are received, and prepare Decision Summary Recommendations for Approving Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Success depends on early communications, detailed planning, and diligent Task Group steering; realistic milestones should be monitored and met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task Group chairperson duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Chairs meetings; oversees preparation of in-house Government cost estimate; maintains objectivity/integrity; establishes and monitors milestones; provides SOW guidance; attends pre-bid/pre-proposal conferences; prepares and forwards Decision Summary Recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chairperson plays a central coordinating and integrity role and must ensure milestones and standards of conduct are observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manpower/Personnel Office duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Notify labor/union representatives; identify Government positions affected; prepare possible Reduction in Force plans; assist displaced Government employees (including possible contractor hiring).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manpower office must handle employee relations, notification, and transition planning as part of the conversion process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional Office duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and prepare the Statement of Work; identify Government Furnished Material (GFM) to be provided to contractor; develop the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functional office is responsible for technical content and performance monitoring constructs that form the basis of both in-house and contractor performance comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller/Financial Office duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare Government cost estimate and conduct the cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial office performs the numerical cost-estimating and comparison activities used to evaluate in-house versus contractor performance costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Office duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Review SOW and solicitation for legal sufficiency; assist in responses to Freedom of Information Act requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal review helps ensure solicitations and SOWs can be defended legally and that statutory obligations (e.g., FOIA) are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Office duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Assure contracting milestones are met; review work specifications; solicit bids/offers; conduct pre-bid/proposal conferences; explain cost procedures; preside at bid openings and determine successful responsive/responsible bids/offers; award contracts; notify appropriate officials in writing upon award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting office must be actively engaged particularly in milestone planning, SOW preparation, and maintaining integrity of the competitive process; reluctance to be involved can lead to poor SOWs and contracting problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Office early involvement in SOW development
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers should be significantly involved early in developing specifications and planning to avoid poorly prepared work statements and ill-defined milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of involvement has led to ambiguous or outdated SOWs that force Contracting Officers to rewrite SOWs and cause delays; attendance at initial Task Group planning meetings is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Milestone planning and solicitation-method impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Milestones must reflect the chosen solicitation method; formally advertised procedures (including small business restricted advertising) are generally quickest; Two-Step Formal Advertising and negotiated procurements (including 8(a) set-asides) tend to lengthen the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-Step requires technical proposal evaluation before priced bids; negotiated/8(a) procurements require cost/pricing data submission and auditing/negotiation which typically take longer; adjust milestones (e.g., one-year vs three-year cost comparison) and expected durations accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award surveys and clearance considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-award surveys, security clearances, and Equal Employment Opportunity clearances may be necessary prior to award; security clearances can significantly delay contract award (interim clearances ~30 days; full up to 60 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting Officers should account for these lead times in milestone planning and coordinate early to avoid award delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Officer responsibility to adhere to milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the purchase request is received, Contracting Officers are expected to adhere to proposed milestones and should carefully analyze their input to milestone planning to ensure they can perform according to schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key to adherence is sound planning and the condition/quality of the SOW when received; poor SOWs can lead to significant schedule slips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Work (SOW) core requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: SOW must be accurate, performance-oriented, written around the same scope and performance level regardless of who performs the work, and sufficiently precise to avoid misinterpretation; must include performance standards monitorable for both in-house and contract performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SOW should indicate what is to be done (not how), provide methods of evaluating performance, describe duties/tasks/responsibilities, identify required facilities/materials, use historical data for variable workload estimates, and identify Government Furnished Facilities/Materials/Equipment where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: SOW and surveillance plan linkage
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation of the SOW and the surveillance plan must be coordinated — desired performance levels, assessment methods, and criteria for acceptable or deficient performance are key ingredients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of definitive performance standards or surveillance plans observed during reviews indicates need for early Contracting Officer involvement to ensure usable documents for solicitation and contract administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commanding Officer certification on most efficient organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanding Officer must certify that the cost comparison will be based on the most efficient organization for in-house operation; SOWs should not simply reflect existing position descriptions if they are not the most efficient organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification is a recent requirement and changes how SOWs and in-house estimates are prepared for cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Officer participation in initial planning and use of centralized resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers are encouraged to attend initial planning meetings and review existing materials and centralized SOWs/specifications being compiled by Navy and DoD groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References such as USAF regulations and published guides on writing service contracts can be helpful; providing common deficiencies and centralized outlines to functional activities improves SOW quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain integrity and equitable treatment in cost-comparison process
rubrics_metrics.description: One objective of the Circular and Handbook is equitable and consistent treatment of all interested persons; the appearance of compromise can lead to severe criticism and must be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personnel involved in evaluation/contracting should not access the Government in-house cost estimate until the most favorable offer to the Government has been determined; safeguards and procedures must be established to maintain confidentiality and objectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access restrictions to in-house cost estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel involved in contracting and evaluation must not have access to the Government in-house cost estimate until the most favorable offer has been determined; violations undermine integrity and may cause audit difficulties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: during an 8(a) procurement many contracting office representatives learned the in-house estimate before the most favorable offer was determined — this is inappropriate. Air Force requires Task Group members to sign Standards of Conduct statements per DOD Directive 5500.7; Chair must advise members on integrity and establish procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Cost Comparison clause — formally advertised solicitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Clause to notify bidders that solicitation is subject to Government cost comparison: in-house cost estimate provided for review at bid opening or as practicable; Government compares in-house estimate to low responsive/responsible bidder; award withheld at least five workdays after bid opening to allow review; three-year cost-estimate basis described (straightline method for 2nd/3rd year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage contracting for three-year periods; if contract less than three years, bidders advised three-year period is for evaluation only. Completed cost comparison made available after award or cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Cost Comparison clause — negotiated solicitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Clause for negotiated solicitations: in-house cost estimate submitted in sealed envelope prior to receipt of priced proposals; after negotiations and determination of most favorable offer, a public opening of the in-house estimate is scheduled; in-house estimate is treated as a 'proposal' for late proposal provisions; award withheld at least five workdays after in-house opening to allow review and appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals must be submitted in writing within five workdays after opening; no final study completion until appeal decision issued and worksheet cost elements validated; cost comparison based on three-year projections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-year cost comparison evaluation methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost comparison is based on a three-year cost estimate: if contractor bid is for one year, it is straightlined for years 2 and 3; appropriate Government costs are similarly straightlined; only items with known changes (excluding inflation) are adjusted for years 2 and 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodology is intended to average out atypical first-year conversion costs; activities encouraged to solicit three-year contracts though evaluation period does not bind offers beyond their stated term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory inclusion of employment/wage-related clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicitations must include clauses relating to equal employment opportunity, veterans preference, minimum wages and fringe benefits, and OFPP Policy Letter No. 78-2 (wage busting), plus clause requiring contractor to offer displaced employees the right of refusal for openings for which they are qualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These clauses protect employee rights in conversions and ensure compliance with applicable labor and policy requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible/emergent local clauses to protect Government interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities have developed local clauses to address conversion-specific risks, such as contractor cooperation with successors for turnover, contractor strike contingency plans, contract price reductions for nonavailability/substandard performance, unbalanced bid evaluation clauses to reject likely buy-ins, and clauses requiring contractor to use the same number of personnel proposed in Step One of Two-Step advertising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legality and enforceability of some local clauses may be questionable; in the absence of specific DAR coverage, Contracting Officers often insert clauses they deem necessary to preserve equity and protect Government interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: DAR coverage limitations and clause proliferation
rubrics_metrics.description: Defense Acquisition Regulation contains limited and piecemeal guidance on service contracting and lacks explicit coverage (e.g., firm/bid rule), resulting in proliferation of clause variations across agencies and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sectional DAR coverage is spread (e.g., buy-ins, options, Service Contract Act, personal services), but only about one percent of DAR is devoted to service contracts; DAR Council has recognized desirability of separate service contract coverage.
